analysis.description: This paper presents a novel approach called Haptics-based Curiosity (HaC) that uses mismatches in haptic feedback to guide exploration in sparse-reward reinforcement learning tasks. It introduces the MiniTouch benchmark of simulated tasks to evaluate the method's performance. The study compares HaC against other curiosity-based exploration methods and shows that it is more sample-efficient and performs better in robot interaction tasks.

name.justification: The paper focuses on reinforcement learning tasks, particularly in the context of haptic feedback and exploration.
name.quote: Robots in many real-world settings have access to force/torque sensors in their gripper and tactile sensing is often necessary for tasks that involve contact-rich motion. In this work, we leverage surprise from mismatches in haptics feedback to guide exploration in hard sparse-reward reinforcement learning tasks.
